Epoxy resin starts as a liquid and hardens through a chemical reaction between resin and hardener, not by drying or cooling.
Resin dates back thousands of years - ancient Egyptians used natural resins and pine sap for waterproofing and embalming.
Most epoxy resin needs 24 to 72 hours to cure fully, even though it may feel dry to the touch much sooner.
Resin can trap air bubbles as it cures, which is why makers often use a heat gun or torch to pop them before it sets.
River tables get their name from the resin river poured between two slabs of wood to mimic flowing water.
